item.title: September 14, 2026 — Morning — September 14, 2026 — The $400 Million Machine Nobody Can Afford to Ignore
item.description: What the hell do you call a machine that costs roughly four hundred million dollars, is basically impossible to replace, and the companies buying it are lining up anyway? Apparently, you call it infrastructure. Good morning. This is SOCIAL SIGNAL, and today we need to talk about something marketers chronically underestimate: the person with the loudest brand is not always the person with the most power.

item.title: September 13, 2026 — Evening — September 13, 2026 — AI Wants to Hit the Brakes and Ring the Nasdaq Bell
item.description: SOCIAL SIGNAL — Evening — September 13, 2026 — AI Wants to Hit the Brakes and Ring the Nasdaq Bell What the fuck do you call it when an AI company says the industry should slow down because the technology may be moving too fast… and then, basically one news cycle later, reportedly picks Nasdaq for a potential IPO? You call it 2026.

item.title: September 13, 2026 — the hell happened to the idea that innovation means adding more stuff
item.description: What the hell happened to the idea that innovation means adding more stuff? Because in Dallas, an entrepreneur is trying to build a new pickup truck company around a surprisingly rebellious proposition: what if a vehicle just… did vehicle things? No rolling movie theater. No dashboard that looks like someone glued an iPad Pro to a refrigerator.

item.title: September 12, 2026 — Evening — September 12, 2026 — When a Flag Becomes a Shopping Filter
item.description: What the hell happens when the little “Made in…” line on a package suddenly becomes more persuasive than the price tag? Because that is happening in Canada right now, and if you work in marketing, you should pay attention. Not because we are about to turn the produce aisle into a geopolitical seminar.

item.title: September 12, 2026 — Morning — September 12, 2026 — The Infinite Scroll Is Going on Trial
item.description: What the fuck happens to digital marketing when one of the most successful product features ever invented starts looking less like brilliant UX and more like something regulators want to put behind caution tape? Because this morning, the humble infinite scroll has a lawyer problem.

item.title: September 11, 2026 — Evening — September 11, 2026 — Meta Tried to Buy an Ad on TikTok. TikTok Said Nope.
item.description: What the fuck happens when one social platform tries to buy ads on another social platform… to pressure that platform into joining its multibillion-dollar child-safety settlement? Apparently, you get the corporate equivalent of walking into your rival’s house, asking to borrow their microphone, and announcing that they should really rethink their life choices.

item.title: September 11, 2026 — Morning — September 11, 2026 — Zara Is Letting Your Cart Pick Its Next Store
item.description: SOCIAL SIGNAL — Morning — September 11, 2026 — Zara Is Letting Your Cart Pick Its Next Store What the fuck happens when your online shopping cart becomes a real-estate consultant? Because that is basically what Zara’s parent company is doing in the United States. Inditex is using online-order patterns to help decide where physical stores should go next.

item.title: September 10, 2026 — The Internet Is Being Sued for Being Too Good at Its Job
item.description: SOCIAL SIGNAL September 10, 2026 — Evening Edition What happens when the most successful product feature in modern media becomes the thing people start suing you for? Because that is basically where we are tonight. Infinite scroll, autoplay, notifications, hyper-personalized recommendations — the machinery marketers have spent years learning to exploit for reach and retention — is now being challenged in court as potentially too effective at keeping human beings engaged.

item.title: SOCIAL SIGNAL — Morning — September 10, 2026 — Apple Just Made Foldables Mainstream
item.description:
Apple just pushed foldables closer to the mainstream—and that is only one part of what changed today.
In this episode of SOCIAL SIGNAL, we break down the biggest shifts in marketing, AI, tech, media, consumer behavior, and culture, then pull out the signals marketers should actually care about.
Expect clear facts, sharp WTF moments, and practical takeaways on brand strategy, attention, search, social media, positioning, and where consumer behavior may be heading next.
SOCIAL SIGNAL is the daily marketing briefing for people who want to understand what happened, why it matters, and what marketers should do with it. Follow this podcast and @socialwithrob on Instagram for more marketing secrets.
